key_agent_trends: EU advances tech sovereignty with proposal for Quantum Act and Sovereign Tech Equity Fund to scale critical AI and quantum investments.
AI Act enforcement progresses as AI Office reviews second-round incident replies from OpenAI and Anthropic on loss-of-control cases.
European semiconductor efforts continue with Dutch Axelera AI seeking $400M for AI inference chips amid IPCEI subsidy talks.
Horizon Europe allocates €297 million for frontier AI, robotics, energy-efficient data centres and distributed processing to reduce dependencies.

stories.headline: European Commission proposes Quantum Act and Sovereign Tech Equity Fund
stories.what_happened: On 25 November 2026 the European Commission proposed the Quantum Act to convert Europe's quantum research into industrial capacity, strengthen supply chains and prepare digital systems for post-quantum cryptography. The proposal lays the groundwork for the Sovereign Tech Equity Fund (STEF) to deliver equity and similar financing for technologies essential to technological sovereignty and economic security, including AI, quantum, cybersecurity, biotech and chips. No fixed budget is allocated in the proposal; reports citing officials have referenced a target scale of up to €50 billion.
stories.why_it_matters: Seeks to address Europe's scale-up capital gap and accelerate industrialisation of strategic technologies critical for AI sovereignty and competitiveness.

stories.headline: EU AI Office receives second-round replies from OpenAI and Anthropic on AI incidents
stories.what_happened: On 25 November 2026 a European Commission spokesperson confirmed that OpenAI and Anthropic submitted replies on 24 November to a second request for information from the AI Office. The second request sought details on the number of AI incidents and how many affected the EU after initial replies omitted the figures. The AI Office is assessing the answers; no specific numbers or assessment timetable have been disclosed. The process follows earlier inquiries related to loss-of-control and containment incidents.
stories.why_it_matters: Marks concrete progress in AI Act enforcement for general-purpose AI providers, testing obligations around incident reporting and risk management.

stories.headline: Dutch AI chipmaker Axelera AI in talks to raise $400 million
stories.what_happened: Bloomberg reported that Eindhoven-based Axelera AI is in talks to raise an additional $400 million to expand development of its specialised AI inference semiconductors. The company is also seeking several hundred million euros in grants through the EU's Important Projects of Common European Interest (IPCEI) programme. Axelera, backed by BlackRock and Samsung Catalyst, develops energy-efficient processors for edge, enterprise and data-centre inference workloads. No valuation or confirmed new investors have been disclosed; discussions remain ongoing.
stories.why_it_matters: Supports European efforts to develop sovereign AI hardware capacity in the inference segment, reducing reliance on non-European suppliers.

stories.headline: European Commission opens €297 million Horizon Europe calls for AI and tech sovereignty
stories.what_happened: On 17 November 2026 the European Commission opened two Horizon Europe calls with a combined indicative budget of €297 million under the Digital, Industry and Space work programme. Four AI topics totalling €107 million cover frontier AI with safety by design, AI-enabled robotics, sectoral uptake and international cooperation. A further €112 million targets distributed energy-efficient AI processing, 3C infrastructure and sustainable AI data centres. Proposals are due by 18 March 2027.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides dedicated research funding to strengthen European AI capabilities, improve infrastructure sustainability and reduce external technological dependencies.
